newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese minister says urban population crippling.
newsitem.headline: Chinese minister says urban population crippling.

text.p: The vast burden of China's population is crippling urbanisation and social and economic development, state media on Tuesday quoted Construction Minister Hou Jie as saying.
China's urban population was expected to hit 450 million by the year 2000 as rural labourers poured in from the countryside, the official China Daily quoted Hou as saying.

"The vast burden of the population combined with the shortage of resources will cripple urbanisation and socio-economic development for some time to come," the newspaper quoted the construction minister as saying.
Much had been done to boost housing construction, but the speed of urbanisation would remain constant for some time, Hou said, but gave no details.

More than 33 million square metres (355 million square feet) of shabby Chinese housing were in urgent need of renovation, while around 45 percent of urban homes had inadequate kitchen and toilet facilities, he said.

Over the past five years, a total of 1.3 billion square metres (14.0 billion square feet) of urban housing had been built, with average per capita urban living space hitting 7.9 square metres (85.0 square feet), the Xinhua news agency reported.

A further 1.2 billion square metres (12.9 billion square feet) of housing would be built over the next five years to boost average living space to 9.0 square metres (96.9 square feet) by the year 2000, it said.
China officially restricts urban residency but has found it almost impossible to slow a wave of rural migrants flocking to seek jobs in more prosperous urban areas.
Beijing says about 80 million surplus rural labourers have left their villages in the last few years to find work in cities and towns, putting increasing strain on urban infrastructure and society.
